lines.name: South Bay Line

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to San Diego Bay speed rules
segments.constraint: Posted 5 mph area in South San Diego Bay south of Loews Resort / Sweetwater Channel (pylon-marked wildlife-refuge water) caps the first ~2–3 nm out of Chula Vista
segments.routing: Exit Safe Harbor South Bay at marina speed and hold the marked channel north through the posted South Bay 5 mph zone (cement pylons; wildlife refuges, sea-turtle habitat and shoals outside the channel) until clear of Loews Resort / Sweetwater Channel; then full-speed main-channel water up the central bay — passing under the Coronado Bridge navigation span, standing clear of the Bay Bridge mooring/roadstead 5 mph area, the 33 CFR 165.1101 security-zone shore off 32nd St, and §334.880 naval anchorages — to the Fifth Avenue Landing approach.

Short main-channel hop along the downtown Embarcadero; no general speed limit in the main channel (SDUPD Port Code §4.35(c)(3)); mind cruise-ship movements at B Street Pier and harbor-tour traffic; marina/berth speeds at the pier faces only.

lines.phase_notes: Flagship corridor. ~30–40 min Chula Vista↔downtown indicative end-to-end INCLUDING the 5 mph South Bay tail, vs a 15–60 min I-5 drive. Anchored by Gaylord Pacific (walking distance from the Chula Vista landing) on the reverse commute + downtown/Convention Center employers on the forward run. The demand signal is brand new and proven — a public commuter ferry launched on this exact pair June 1, 2026 — and Navier's employer seat-block overlay adds guaranteed seats and frequency as a complement to it, never a displacement (incumbent_respect_flagship governs all copy).

lines.name: Point Loma Line

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to San Diego Bay speed rules
segments.constraint: Short basin-to-basin hop dominated by Shelter Island / America's Cup Harbor basin and marina speed limits — no meaningful open-water segment
segments.routing: Round the Shelter Island mole between the guest docks and America's Cup Harbor at basin speeds; all inside-basin water.

Exit America's Cup Harbor and run the north-bay main channel east: full-speed water (no general main-channel limit, SDUPD §4.35(c)(3)); stay in/near the marked channel clear of the Point Loma naval-shore zones (33 CFR 165.1102; §334.870 degaussing-station most-direct-transit rule) and the §334.880 anchorage; enter the Harbor Island basin at marina speed.
Short full-speed hop from the Harbor Island basin east along the main channel to the Broadway Pier face; marina-basin speeds on exit only.

lines.phase_notes: Phase 2 premium residential play: the highest verified catchment income in the market (Point Loma 92106, $142,897) into the downtown core, ~15–25 min indicative, essentially all full-speed water — and NO incumbent scheduled service exists on this pair. Harbor Island is the authored opportunistic infill stop; it carries no airport story (see its note_internal — the 2025 entrance road already solved most of that pain, and no landing serves the terminals).

lines.name: Bridge Line

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to San Diego Bay speed rules
segments.constraint: 5 mph inside Glorietta Bay (SDUPD Port Code §4.35(c)(3)) plus the Bay Bridge mooring/roadstead 5 mph area on the crossing
segments.routing: Exit Glorietta Bay at 5 mph, pass through the Coronado Bridge navigation span, cross the main channel standing clear of the Bay Bridge mooring/roadstead 5 mph area, and approach Fifth Avenue Landing at berth speed.

lines.phase_notes: Coronado Bridge bypass feeder — Coronado residents into the Convention Center / Gaslamp core without the bridge. Deliberately anchored at Glorietta Bay — NOT at the incumbent ferry's Coronado landing — to complement (not clone) the existing subsidized Coronado ferry (see decision_ledger). The crossing is below the 20-min sweet spot and partly speed-constrained — bundle as a feeder with NO numeric time claim; a City of Coronado / incumbent-partner conversation gates this line.

copy.hero_headline: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network.
copy.hero_sub: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network. Navier is building an employer water network for San Diego Bay — 30-seat electric hydrofoils linking Chula Vista's new bayfront, the Convention Center, and downtown's Broadway Pier at launch, growing to Shelter Island, Point Loma, Harbor Island, and Glorietta Bay. One protected bay, twelve miles of fast water, and a commute that skips the bridge and the freeway.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · first service no earlier than end-2027 · complements the bay's existing ferry
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: The bridge and the freeway are the chokepoints. The bay is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: San Diego's bayfront commute funnels through two chokepoints: the Coronado Bridge — roughly 75,000 vehicles a day, where a physical barrier still gets moved twice daily to flip a lane with the commute — and the I-5 South corridor, where a 15-minute free-flow drive from Chula Vista routinely stretches far longer at rush hour. The bay itself is the alternative: twelve nautical miles of protected water running straight past every major bayfront job cluster, with fast, open water in the main channel. And San Diego already commutes by water — a commuter ferry has crossed to Coronado every weekday morning for three decades, and a new Chula Vista run launched in 2026. The water works. We add guaranteed seats and new stations.

copy.network_lead: At launch, one flagship corridor: the South Bay Line — Chula Vista Bayfront · Convention Center (Fifth Avenue Landing) · Broadway Pier — about 30–40 minutes end to end (indicative), anchored by the Gaylord Pacific resort at walking distance from the Chula Vista landing. Phase 2 adds the Point Loma Line — Shelter Island · America's Cup Harbor · Harbor Island · Broadway Pier, about 15–25 minutes (indicative) — the bay's highest-income catchment, with no scheduled water service on that pair today. Phase 3 adds the Bridge Line, a Glorietta Bay ↔ Convention Center feeder giving Coronado a bridge-free crossing. Phase 2 and 3 stations render as planned, not promised.
copy.network_footnote: San Diego's ferry operator has served this bay for over a century, and its commuter runs prove the market every weekday. Navier's network is designed as a complement — guaranteed employer seat blocks, new station pairs like Point Loma and Glorietta Bay, and more frequency where today's schedule is light — never a replacement. Chula Vista's bayfront is the fastest-growing employer story on the bay. The Gaylord Pacific Resort & Convention Center opened in May 2025 with 1,600 rooms and roughly 800 hires at opening — and thousands more jobs are projected as the bayfront district builds out — all at walking distance from the water. Employer seat blocks there fill the reverse commute; downtown, Convention Center, and Gaslamp employers fill the forward run. South Bay times include the posted 5 mph channel tail (indicative).

decision_ledger.status: real active ferry stop — NOT authored as a station; partner conversation first
decision_ledger.reason: Flagship's Coronado service is subsidized and free at commute hours (City-funded runs 4:50–8:30 AM since 1993) and goes electric fall 2026 — any Navier landing there reads head-to-head. The retail-center lease is also in flux (40-yr lease expired June 30, 2026; Port board voted a one-year renewal June 23, 2026; $20M revitalization on hold). Coronado is served instead via the Phase-3 Glorietta Bay feeder. Revisit ONLY inside an operating-partner conversation with Flagship / the Port / the City (coronado_lease_internal).

Inventory kills it: a subsidized incumbent that is free at commute hours and converting to electric ferries. Navier never renders, implies, or reserves this pair. Differentiation lives on employer seat blocks, foil speed, and unserved pairs.

decision_ledger.topic: National City Line (Pier 32 Marina ↔ Fifth Avenue Landing / Broadway Pier)
decision_ledger.status: real marina, corridor held — inventoried, NOT routed
decision_ledger.reason: ~4.5 nm of all-speed water, but walk-tier employment is weak at both ends (the 32nd St gates are shuttle-tier, ~1.5–2 mi from Pier 32) and National City catchment income is unverified. Hold until a base-shuttle partnership or a Barrio Logan float exists; then revisit as a feeder.

The demand story is real and sourced (the City's own feasibility study proposes a pedestrian bridge just to manage shift-change flows on Harbor Drive), but there is NO civilian landing in Barrio Logan. Requires a new permitted float at/near Cesar Chavez Park (watchlist; Port park-improvement process live in 2026). Never render.

Fifth Avenue Landing is an active ferry stop with transient berthing and both incumbent routes landing there — the proven Convention Center gate. Marriott Marquis Marina (445 slips; 3 guest slips 30–65 ft) is the inventoried alternate gate if Fifth Avenue Landing berth terms fail.

decision_ledger.topic: Coronado Cays / Loews Crown Isle marinas
decision_ledger.reason: Both sit at the edge of (or inside) the posted South Bay 5 mph zone with residential-only catchment (resident counts unknown) and a thin employer base (Loews resort only, headcount unknown). Watch as a possible future residential-feeder overlay on the South Bay Line; do not render.
